analysis.investment_thesis: IXIGO operates an asset-light OTA business with an interesting tier-2/3 India niche and strong FCF conversion in FY25, but ROCE of 12.6% fails my 15% threshold and the market is charging 133x trailing earnings for a 7% operating margin business. At this price, there is no margin of safety whatsoever.
key_strengths: Asset-light model with 81.7% gross margins and near-zero debt (D/E: 0.04), showing genuine capital efficiency at the gross level
Strong revenue trajectory: ₹40 Cr (2019) → ₹914 Cr (2025), 68.5% CAGR, with FCF turning robustly positive at ₹118 Cr in FY25
Defensible train + bus niche (ConfirmTkt, AbhiBus brands) targeting underserved tier-2/3 India travelers where MakeMyTrip is weaker
key_risks: Intensely competitive OTA market with MakeMyTrip/Goibibo having far deeper pockets and brand recall — switching costs for consumers are essentially zero
Operating margins at 7.08% leave no room for error; net profit actually declined from ₹73 Cr (FY24) to ₹60 Cr (FY25) despite 39% revenue growth — margin dilution is happening
ROIC proxies (ROE 9.74%, ROCE 12.60%) are structurally below the 15% floor required to justify a quality premium, let alone a 133x P/E
red_flags: 'Other Income' of ₹39 Cr (FY24) and ₹23 Cr (FY25) is contributing materially to net profit — strip it out and FY24 operating profit was only ₹38 Cr; earnings quality is weaker than headline suggests
Forward P/E of 57x still requires extraordinary growth and margin expansion that is far from guaranteed in a commoditized travel aggregation business
FII ownership at 64.19% creates crowded-trade risk; any global risk-off or re-rating of Indian internet/OTA multiples could compress the stock violently
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Inverting first, as I always do: what would have to go wrong here? Almost everything already is, except the revenue line. The business earns a 7% operating margin in a sector where the dominant player (MakeMyTrip) with far superior scale earns only modestly better margins. IRCTC — the government monopoly on train ticketing — is IXIGO's upstream landlord on its largest volume category. That is not a moat; it is a dependency. ROCE at 12.6% tells me this business is not yet earning its cost of capital on an economic basis, yet the market prices it at 119x EV/EBITDA as though it already is a compounding machine. The math simply does not work.

The FY25 FCF of ₹118 Cr is genuinely encouraging and the balance sheet is clean. But the net profit actually fell from ₹73 Cr to ₹60 Cr year-over-year despite 39% revenue growth — a warning sign that costs are scaling faster than the topline. The reliance on "Other Income" (interest on IPO proceeds, one-time items) to flatter reported profits is precisely the kind of accounting murkiness I find uncomfortable. A great business does not need financial engineering to look profitable. At 133x trailing P/E, the market has priced in a decade of flawless execution in a business with thin margins, fierce competition, and no durable pricing power. I will not pay a premium price for a mediocre moat.
